title.zh: 卷十五 梁書15: 列傳五 韓建 李罕之 馮行襲 孫德昭 趙克裕 張慎思
title.en: Volume 15 Book of Later Liang 15: Biographies 5: Han Jian, Li Hanzhi, Feng Xingxi, Sun Dezhao, Zhao Keyu, Zhang Shensi
title.raw: 卷十五 梁書15: 列傳五 韓建 李罕之 馮行襲 孫德昭 趙克裕 張慎思 Volume 15 Book of Later Liang 15: Biographies 5: Han Jian, Li Hanzhi, Feng Xingxi, Sun Dezhao, Zhao Keyu, Zhang Shensi

sentences.zh: 韓建，字佐時，許州長社人。

translations.literal: Han Jian, style name Zuoshi, was a native of Changshe in Xu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian, styled Zuoshi, came from Changshe in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父叔豐，世為牙校。

translations.literal: His father Shufeng for generations were guard officers.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shufeng served for generations as a guard officer.

sentences.zh: 初，秦宗權之據蔡州，招合亡命，建隸為軍士，累轉至小校。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qin Zongquan held Caizhou, he gathered fugitives; Jian was attached as a soldier and rose through ranks to junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Zongquan held Caizhou he recruited fugitives; Jian joined as a soldier and rose to junior officer.

sentences.zh: 唐中和初，忠武監軍楊復光起兵於蔡，宗權遣其將鹿宴宏赴之，建與里人王建俱隸宴宏軍，入援京師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe of Tang, Zhongwu overseer Yang Fuguang raised troops at Cai; Zongquan sent his general Lu Yanhong to go; Jian and fellow townsman Wang Jian both were attached to Yanhong's army and entered the capital to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhonghe, Yang Fuguang of Zhongwu raised troops at Cai; Jian and townsman Wang Jian marched with Lu Yanhong to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 賊平，復光暴卒。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Fuguang died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels fell, Fuguang died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 時僖宗在蜀，宴宏率所部赴行在。

translations.literal: At that time Xizong was in Shu; Yanhong led his command to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: With Xizong in Shu, Yanhong marched to the court.

sentences.zh: 路出南山，因攻剽郡邑，據有興元。

translations.literal: The road passed through the southern mountains; he therefore raided prefectures and districts and held Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Marching through the Qinling he raided towns and seized Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 宴宏自為留後，以建為蜀郡刺史。

translations.literal: Yanhong made himself acting commissioner and made Jian Shu prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhong made himself commissioner and appointed Jian Shu prefect.

sentences.zh: 唐軍容使田令孜密遣人誘建，啖以厚利，建時懼為宴宏所並，乃率所部歸行在，令孜補為神策都校、金吾將軍，出為潼關防禦使兼華州刺史。

translations.literal: Tang Army Rong Commissioner Tian Lingzi secretly sent men to entice Jian, feeding him rich profit; Jian then feared being absorbed by Yanhong, led his command to return to the traveling palace; Lingzi supplemented him as Shence column commander and Golden Guard general, sent out as Tong Pass defense commissioner and concurrent Hua prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi lured Jian away from Yan Hong with rich promises. Fearing that Yan Hong would absorb him, Jian led his troops back to the traveling court, where Lingzi appointed him Shence column commander and Golden Guard general, then sent him out as Tong Pass defense commissioner and concurrently prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 河、潼經大寇之後，戶口流散，建披荊棘，辟汙萊，勸課農事，樹植蔬果，出入閭裏，親問疾苦，不數年，流亡畢復，軍民充實。

translations.literal: After great banditry in He and Tong, households scattered in flight; Jian cleared brambles, opened foul wasteland, urged farming, planted fruits and vegetables, went in and out of lanes, personally asked of suffering and illness—in several years exiles all returned and army and people were full.
translations.idiomatic: After the ravaging of He and Tong he cleared land, urged farming, and within years restored refugees and prosperity.

sentences.zh: 建比不知書，治郡之暇，日課學習。

translations.literal: Jian by nature did not know books; in leisure from governing the prefecture he daily set lessons in study.
translations.idiomatic: Illiterate at first, he studied daily while governing.

sentences.zh: 遣人於器皿、床榻之上各題其名，建視之既熟，乃漸通文字。

translations.literal: He sent men to label his name on vessels, beds, and couches; when Jian had viewed them until familiar, he gradually penetrated written characters.
translations.idiomatic: He labeled household goods with his name until he learned to read.

sentences.zh: 俄遷華商節度、潼關守捉等使，累加檢校太尉、平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred Hua-Shang military commissioner and Tong Pass guard commissioner and the like, repeatedly raised to honorary Grand Marshal and co-equal chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Hua-Shang commissioner, Tong Pass commander, honorary Grand Marshal, and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，建與鳳翔李茂貞、邠州王行瑜舉兵赴闕，迫昭宗請以王珙為河中帥，害大臣於都下。

translations.literal: In Qianning year 2 Jian with Fengxiang's Li Maozhen and Binzhou's Wang Xingyu raised troops to the capital, forced Zhaozong to make Wang Gong Hezhong commander, and killed great ministers in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qianning 2 he marched with Maozhen and Xingyu on the capital, forced Wang Gong on Hezhong, and killed ministers.

sentences.zh: 河中王珂召晉軍以為援，及晉軍渡河，昭宗幸石門。

translations.literal: Hezhong's Wang Ke called Jin troops as aid; when Jin troops crossed the river, Zhaozong went to Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke called Jin aid; when Jin crossed the river Zhaozong fled to Shimen.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，昭宗遣延王、通王率禁兵討李茂貞，為茂貞所敗，車駕幸渭橋。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of year 3 Zhaozong sent Princes Yan and Tong with palace guard troops to attack Li Maozhen; they were defeated by Maozhen; the imperial carriage reached Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Month 4, year 3, imperial princes attacked Maozhen, were beaten, and the emperor reached Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 翌日，次富平，將幸河中，建奉表迎駕，俄自至渭北，懇乞東幸，許之。

translations.literal: The next day, stopping at Fuping, about to go to Hezhong, Jian submitted a memorial welcoming the carriage; soon he came in person to north of Wei, earnestly begging the eastern journey, and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuping Jian welcomed the emperor and persuaded him east to Hua.

sentences.zh: 七月十五日，昭宗至華下，百官士庶相繼而至。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month Zhaozong reached below Hua; officials and commoners followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Month 7, day 15, the emperor reached Hua with the court in train.

sentences.zh: 建尋加兼中書令，充京畿安撫製置等使，又兼京兆尹、京城把截使。

translations.literal: Jian was soon added concurrent Grand Secretary, full capital-region pacification and disposition commissioner, also concurrent Jingzhao prefect and capital intercept commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He became Grand Secretary, capital pacification commissioner, Jingzhao prefect, and intercept commander.

sentences.zh: 昭宗久在華州，思還宮掖，每花朝月夕，遊宴西溪，與群臣屬詠歌詩，歔欷流涕。

translations.literal: Zhaozong long at Huazhou, thought of returning to the palace; each flower morning and moon evening he toured and feasted at West Creek with ministers, composing songs and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Long at Hua the emperor yearned for the palace and wept at West Creek feasts.

sentences.zh: 建每從容奏曰：「臣為陛下修營大內，結信諸侯，一二年間，必期興復。」

translations.literal: Jian each time calmly memorialized: "Your subject for Your Majesty repairs the great inner palace, knits faith with the feudatories—in one or two years restoration is sure to be expected."
translations.idiomatic: Jian said calmly, "Your servant will repair the great inner palace for Your Majesty and win the feudatories' trust—in one or two years restoration is sure."

sentences.zh: 乃以建兼領修創京城使，建自華督役輦運工作，復治大明宮。

translations.literal: He therefore made Jian concurrently oversee capital repair commissioner; Jian from Hua supervised labor, transport, and work, and again repaired Daming Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He put Jian in charge of rebuilding the capital and Daming Palace from Hua.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，有詣建告睦王已下八王謀殺建，建囚八王於別宅，放散隨駕殿後軍二萬人，殺捧日都頭李筠。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, someone came to Jian reporting that Prince Mu and eight other princes below him plotted to kill Jian; Jian imprisoned the eight princes in a separate residence, discharged the twenty thousand rear palace-guard troops accompanying the emperor, and killed Pengri column chief Li Yun.
translations.idiomatic: In month 2 of the fourth year someone accused eight princes including Prince Mu of plotting against Jian; he imprisoned them, dismissed twenty thousand rear guards, and killed Pengri chief Li Yun.

sentences.zh: 自是天子益微，宿衛之士盡矣。

translations.literal: From this the Son of Heaven grew ever weaker and the palace guards were gone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew weaker still and lost his guards.

sentences.zh: 八月，建以兵圍十六宅，通王以下十一王並遇害於石堤穀，以謀逆聞。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Jian surrounded the Sixteen Residences with troops; Prince Tong and eleven other princes below him were all killed at Shidi Valley, reported as a treason plot.
translations.idiomatic: Month 8 he besieged the Sixteen Residences; Prince Tong and ten other princes were killed at Shidi Valley as alleged traitors.

sentences.zh: 又害太子詹事馬道殷、將作監許岩士，貶宰相朱樸，皆昭宗寵昵者也。

translations.literal: He also killed Crown Prince Administrator Ma Daoyin and Construction Commissioner Xu Yanshi, and demoted Chief Minister Zhu Pu—all men Zhaozong favored.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Ma Daoyin and Xu Yanshi and demoted Zhu Pu, all Zhaozong favorites.

sentences.zh: 建尋兼同州節度使。

translations.literal: Jian soon added concurrent Tongzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jian soon added Tongzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 光化元年，升華州為興德府，以建為尹。

translations.literal: Guanghua year 1, Hua prefecture was elevated to Xingde Prefecture and Jian was made its intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghua 1 elevated Hua to Xingde Prefecture and made Jian its intendant.

sentences.zh: 八月，車駕還京。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Month 8 the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，冊拜太傅，進封許國公，並賜鐵券。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was enfeoffed Grand Tutor, advanced to Duke of Xu, and granted an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: Month 9 he became Grand Tutor, Duke of Xu, and received an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 天復元年十一月，宦官韓全誨迫天子幸鳳翔，建亦預其謀。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Tianfu year 1 eunuch Han Quanhui forced the Son of Heaven to go to Fengxiang; Jian also shared the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu 1, month 11, Han Quanhui seized the emperor for Fengxiang; Jian helped.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，自河中引軍而西。

translations.literal: The Founder heard it and led troops from Hezhong west.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder marched west from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 前鋒至同州，建判官司馬鄴以城降，遂移軍迫華州，建懼乞降。

translations.literal: The vanguard reached Tongzhou; Jian's aide Sima Ye surrendered the city; he then shifted troops to press Huazhou; Jian in fear begged surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sim Ye surrendered Tongzhou; the Founder besieged Hua and Jian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 太祖責以脅君之罪，建拜伏稱從事李巨川之謀也，太祖即誅巨川。

translations.literal: The Founder blamed him for coercing the sovereign; Jian bowed prostrate and said it was follower Li Juchuan's plot; the Founder at once executed Juchuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder blamed him for intimidating the throne; Jian blamed Li Juchuan and the Founder killed Juchuan.

sentences.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》：韓建曰：「某不識字，凡朝廷章奏、鄰封書檄，皆巨川為之。」

translations.literal: (The 《Fragmentary Tales of the Northern Dream》: Han Jian said: "I do not know characters; all court memorials and neighboring letters were done by Juchuan."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Northern Dream》 says Jian admitted, "I cannot read; Juchuan wrote all my court papers and neighboring letters."

sentences.zh: 因斬之。

translations.literal: Therefore he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: So he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 《新唐書· 李巨川傳》云：巨川詣軍門納款，因言當世利害。

translations.literal: The 《New Book of Tang · Biography of Li Juchuan》 says: Juchuan came to the army gate to submit and spoke on current benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: The 《New Book of Tang》 says Juchuan came to submit and argued policy.

sentences.zh: 全忠屬官敬翔以文翰事左右，疑巨川用則全忠待己或衰，乃詭說曰：「巨川誠奇才，顧不利主人，若何！」

translations.literal: Quanzhong's officer Jing Xiang handled documents at his side and suspected if Juchuan were used Quanzhong's treatment of himself might decline, and therefore spoke deceitfully: "Juchuan is truly a rare talent, but he is not good to his lord—what then!"
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang feared rivalry and told Quanzhong, "Juchuan is truly a rare talent, but he is not good to his lord—what then!"

sentences.zh: 是日，全忠殺之。）〉

translations.literal: That day Quanzhong killed him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: That day Quanzhong killed him.)〉

sentences.zh: 太祖與建素有軍中昆弟之契，及見，其怒驟息，尋表建為許州節度使。

translations.literal: The Founder and Jian from old had army brotherhood pact; when he saw him his anger suddenly ceased; soon he memorialized Jian as Xu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Old army brothers, they reconciled and Jian became Xu commissioner.

sentences.zh: 昭宗東遷，以建為佑國軍節度使、京兆尹。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong moved east, he made Jian Youguo military commissioner and Jingzhao prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved east Jian became Youguo commissioner and Jingzhao prefect.

sentences.zh: 車駕至陝，召太祖與建侍宴，宮妓奏樂，何皇后舉觴以賜太祖，建躡足，太祖遽起曰：「臣醉不任。」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Shan, the Founder and Jian were summoned to attend a feast; palace performers played music; Empress He raised a cup to bestow on the Founder; Jian trod on his foot; the Founder hastily rose saying: "Your subject is drunk and cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: At a feast in Shan the empress toasted the Founder; Jian trod his foot and the Founder hastily rose saying, "Your subject is drunk and cannot bear it."

sentences.zh: 偽若顛仆即去。

translations.literal: He pretended as if to fall headlong and went away.
translations.idiomatic: He staggered away as if drunk.

sentences.zh: 建私謂太祖曰：「上與宮人附耳而語，幕下有兵仗聲，恐圖王爾。」

translations.literal: Jian privately told the Founder: "The sovereign and palace people speak ear to ear; below the curtain there is the sound of weapons—perhaps they plot against you, Prince."
translations.idiomatic: Jian whispered to the Founder, "The emperor and empress are whispering; I heard weapons beneath the curtain—they may be plotting against you."

sentences.zh: 天祐三年，改青州節度使。

translations.literal: In Tianyou year 3 he was changed to Qing military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 3 he was made Qing commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，征為司徒、平章事，充諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication he was summoned as Minister of Works and co-equal chief minister, full commissioner of salt and iron transport for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: At the abdication he became Minister of Works, chief minister, and salt-and-iron transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開平二年，加侍中，充建昌宮使。

translations.literal: In Kaiping year 2 he was made Palace Secretary and full Jianchang Palace commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiping 2 he became Palace Secretary and Jianchang Palace commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，郊祀於洛，以建為大禮使。

translations.literal: In year 3 suburban sacrifice at Luo, he made Jian great rites commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Year 3 he directed the Luo suburban rites.

sentences.zh: 建為上宰，每謁見，時有直言。

translations.literal: Jian as chief minister at each audience sometimes spoke straight words.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he sometimes spoke bluntly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太祖為性剛嚴，群下將迎不暇，待建稍異，故優容之。

translations.literal: The Founder by nature was stern and strict; subordinates could not answer in time; toward Jian he was slightly different, therefore indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: The stern Founder indulged Jian more than other ministers.

sentences.zh: 九月，冊拜太保，罷知政事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was enfeoffed Grand Preceptor and dismissed from knowing government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Month 9 he became Grand Preceptor and left the government.

sentences.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：開平三年十月，詔曰：太保韓建，每月旦、十五日入閣稱賀，即令赴朝參，餘時弗入見。

translations.literal: (The 《Institutes of the Five Dynasties》: Kaiping year 3, tenth month, edict: Grand Preceptor Han Jian on the first and fifteenth of each month enters the hall to offer congratulations, then attends court audience; at other times he does not enter to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Five Dynasties Institutes》 records limited court appearances as special favor.)

sentences.zh: 示優禮也。）〉

translations.literal: Showing preferential courtesy.)〉
translations.idiomatic: A mark of favor.)〉

sentences.zh: 四年三月，除匡國軍節度使、陳許蔡觀察使，仍令中書不議除替。

translations.literal: In the third month of year 4 he was made Kuangguo military commissioner and Chen-Xu-Cai surveillance commissioner, still ordering the Secretariat not to discuss replacement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year, he took Kuangguo and Chen-Xu-Cai with a pledge of no replacement.

sentences.zh: 〈（《五代會要》：乾化元年正月，敕：許昌雄鎮，太保韓建，朕用以布政，民耕盜止，久居其位，庶可勝殘矣。

translations.literal: (The 《Institutes of the Five Dynasties》: Qianhua year 1, first month, edict: Xuchang, the mighty post—Grand Preceptor Han Jian, whom We use to spread government, the people plow and bandits stop; long in the post, he may overcome cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Institutes》 praises his rule at Xuchang and forbids replacement.)

sentences.zh: 宜令中書門下不計年月，勿議替。）〉

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the Secretariat and Chancellery not to count months and not discuss replacement.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The court would not discuss replacing him.)〉

sentences.zh: 乾化二年六月，朝廷新有內難，人心動搖，部將張厚因作亂，害建於衙署，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of Qianhua year 2 the court newly had inner turmoil, hearts were shaken, and subordinate Zhang Hou because of it made disorder and killed Jian in the yamen at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Qianhua 2, month 6, subordinate Zhang Hou murdered Jian in the yamen at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子從訓，昭宗在華時授太子侍學，賜名文禮，尋拜屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Congxun, while Zhaozong was at Hua, was appointed crown prince study companion, granted the name Wenli, and soon made Director of Fields outer-office attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Son Congxun, renamed Wenli, served as crown prince tutor at Hua and became Director of Fields.

sentences.zh: 國初為都官郎中，賜紫，年未弱冠。

translations.literal: At the dynasty's founding he was Capital Crimes bureau director, granted purple, not yet weak cap.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty he was Capital Crimes director with purple robes before twenty.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷命從訓告國哀於陳、許，至二日軍亂，與建並命。

translations.literal: At that time the court ordered Congxun to announce national mourning at Chen and Xu; on the second day army disorder, he died with Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to announce mourning at Chen and Xu, he died in the same mutiny as his father.

sentences.zh: 乾化三年，追贈太師。

translations.literal: In Qianhua year 3 he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Qianhua 3 he was posthumously named Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 李罕之，陳州項城人。

translations.literal: Li Hanzhi was a Xiangcheng man of Chen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi came from Xiangcheng in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 父文，世田家。

translations.literal: His father Wen for generations were farming families.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wen was a farming family for generations.

sentences.zh: 罕之拳勇趫捷，力兼數人。

translations.literal: Hanzhi was fist-brave, nimble, and swift; his strength matched several men.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi was a fierce fighter of several men's strength.

sentences.zh: 少學為儒，不成，又落發為僧，以其無賴，所至不容。

translations.literal: In youth he studied to be a Ruist; it did not succeed; he again shaved his head and became a monk; because he was unruly, wherever he went he was not tolerated.
translations.idiomatic: He failed as a scholar, became a monk, and was driven out everywhere for unruliness.

sentences.zh: 曾乞食於酸棗縣，自旦至晡，無與之者，乃擲缽於地，毀棄僧衣，亡命為盜。

translations.literal: Once he begged food at Suozao county from dawn to dusk with none giving; he then threw his bowl to the ground, destroyed and cast off monk's robes, and fled as an outlaw to become a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Begging all day at Suozao without alms, he smashed his bowl, cast off his robes, and became a bandit.

sentences.zh: 會黃巢起曹、濮，罕之因合徒作剽，漸至魁首。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao rose in Cao and Pu, Hanzhi therefore joined followers in raiding and gradually reached chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao rose he raided and became a bandit chief.

sentences.zh: 及賊巢渡江，罕之因以兵將背賊歸於唐，高駢錄其功，表為光州刺史。

translations.literal: When bandit Chao crossed the river, Hanzhi therefore with troops turned his back on the bandits and returned to Tang; Gao Pian recorded his merit and memorialized him Guang prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao crossed the Yangzi he defected to Tang; Gao Pian made him Guang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，為蔡賊秦宗權寇迫，不能守，乃棄郡歸項城，收合餘眾，依河陽諸葛爽，爽署為懷州刺史。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was harried by Cai bandit Qin Zongquan and could not hold it; he then abandoned the prefecture and returned to Xiangcheng, gathered remnant masses, relied on Heyang's Zhuge Shuang, and Shuang appointed him Huai prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zongquan drove him from Guang; he regrouped at Xiangcheng and Zhuge Shuang made him Huai commissioner.

sentences.zh: 光啟初，僖宗以爽為東南面招討，以擊宗權，爽乃表罕之為副，令將兵屯宋州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangqi, Xizong made Shuang southeast campaign commander to strike Zongquan; Shuang then memorialized Hanzhi as deputy and ordered him to lead troops encamped at Song prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi opened with Shuang campaigning against Zongquan and posting Hanzhi at Song.

sentences.zh: 蔡寇凶焰日熾，兵鋒不敵。

translations.literal: Cai bandits' ferocious flame daily grew keener; military edge could not match.
translations.idiomatic: Cai armies grew too strong to face.

sentences.zh: 中和四年，爽表罕之為河南尹、東都留守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhonghe, Shuang memorialized Hanzhi as Henan prefect and eastern capital acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonghe 4 Shuang made him Henan prefect and eastern capital regent.

sentences.zh: 是歲，李克用脫上源之難，斂軍西歸，路由洛陽，罕之迎謁，供帳館待甚優，因與克用厚相結托。

translations.literal: That year Li Keyong escaped the Shangyuan crisis, gathered troops and returned west; the road passed Luoyang; Hanzhi welcomed and attended, provisions and lodge reception very generous, and therefore thickly joined trust with Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: That year he lavishly hosted Keyong passing through Luoyang and bonded with him.

sentences.zh: 時罕之有眾三千，以聖善寺為府。

translations.literal: At that time Hanzhi had masses three thousand, taking Shengyi Monastery as headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He held three thousand men at Shengyi Monastery.

sentences.zh: 光啟元年，蔡賊秦宗權遣將孫儒來攻，罕之對壘數月，以兵少備竭，委城而遁，西保於澠池。

translations.literal: In Guangqi year 1, Cai bandit Qin Zongquan sent general Sun Ru to attack; Hanzhi faced the camp several months; because soldiers were few and stores exhausted, he abandoned the city and fled, west guarding at Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi 1 Sun Ru besieged Luoyang; outnumbered, Hanzhi fled to Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊據京城月餘，焚燒宮闕，剽剝居民。

translations.literal: Cai bandits held the capital more than a month, burned palace halls, and plundered residents.
translations.idiomatic: Cai rebels held the capital a month, burning palaces and looting the people.

sentences.zh: 賊既退去，鞠為煨燼，寂無雞犬之音。

translations.literal: When the bandits had withdrawn, it was kneaded to embers; silent without chicken or dog sound.
translations.idiomatic: They left only ashes and silence.

sentences.zh: 罕之復引其眾，築壘於市西。

translations.literal: Hanzhi again led his masses and built ramparts west of the market.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi rebuilt camps west of the market.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，諸葛爽死，其將劉經推爽子仲方為帥，經懼罕之難製，自引兵鎮洛陽。

translations.literal: The next winter Zhuge Shuang died; his general Liu Jing pushed Shuang's son Zhongfang as commander; Jing feared Hanzhi hard to control and himself led troops to garrison Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuang died Liu Jing held Luoyang and feared Hanzhi.

sentences.zh: 罕之部曲有李瑭、郭璆者，情不相葉，欲相圖害，罕之怒，誅璆，軍情由是不睦。

translations.literal: Hanzhi's officers Li Tang and Guo Qiu were not on good terms and wished to harm each other; Hanzhi in anger executed Qiu; army hearts from this were not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He killed officer Guo Qiu and lost the army's trust.

sentences.zh: 劉經因其有間，掩擊罕之於澠池。

translations.literal: Liu Jing took advantage of the rift and struck Hanzhi at Mianchi in ambush.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jing ambushed him at Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 軍亂，保乾壕。

translations.literal: The army was in disorder and guarded at Qianhao.
translations.idiomatic: Defeated, he held Qianhao.

sentences.zh: 經急攻之，為罕之所敗，罕之乘勝追至洛陽。

translations.literal: Jing urgently attacked; he was defeated by Hanzhi; Hanzhi took victory in pursuit to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He beat Jing back and pursued to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時經保敬愛寺，罕之保苑中飛龍廄。

translations.literal: At that time Jing guarded Jing'ai Monastery; Hanzhi guarded Flying Dragon Stable in the imperial park.
translations.idiomatic: Jing held Jing'ai Monastery; Hanzhi held the imperial stable.

sentences.zh: 罕之激勵其眾攻敬愛寺，數日，因風縱火，盡燔之，經眾奔竄，追斬殆盡。

translations.literal: Hanzhi roused his masses to attack Jing'ai Monastery; after several days, taking advantage of wind he set fire and burned it all; Jing's troops fled scattered; pursuit beheaded nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: He burned Jing'ai Monastery and slaughtered Jing's army.

sentences.zh: 罕之進逼河陽，營於鞏縣，陳舟於汜水，將渡，諸葛仲方遣將張言率師拒於河上。

translations.literal: Hanzhi advanced to press Heyang, camped at Gong county, arrayed boats at Sishui intending to cross; Zhuge Zhongfang sent general Zhang Yan with troops to resist on the river.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Heyang from Gong and crossed toward Sishui until Zhang Yan blocked the river.

sentences.zh: 時仲方年幼，政在劉經，諸將心多不附。

translations.literal: At that time Zhongfang was young; government was in Liu Jing's hands; the generals' hearts mostly did not attach.
translations.idiomatic: Young Zhongfang was ruled by Liu Jing; the officers were divided.

sentences.zh: 張言密與罕之修好；

translations.literal: Zhang Yan secretly made good relations with Hanzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan secretly allied with Hanzhi;

sentences.zh: 經知其謀，言懼，引眾渡河歸罕之，因合勢攻河陽，為經所敗，罕之與言退保懷州。

translations.literal: Jing knew his plot; Yan in fear led masses across the river to return to Hanzhi, and together attacked Heyang; they were defeated by Jing; Hanzhi and Yan retreated to guard Huai prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan crossed to Hanzhi; together they attacked Heyang, lost, and fled to Huai.

sentences.zh: 冬，蔡將孫儒陷河陽。

translations.literal: In winter, Cai general Sun Ru took Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Winter brought Sun Ru's capture of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 仲方泛輕舟來奔，孫儒遂自稱節度使。

translations.literal: Zhongfang came fleeing in a light boat; Sun Ru then declared himself military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfang fled by boat; Sun Ru seized Heyang.

sentences.zh: 俄而蔡賊為我軍所敗，孫儒棄河陽歸蔡。

translations.literal: Soon Cai bandits were defeated by our army; Sun Ru abandoned Heyang and returned to Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Soon our armies beat Cai and Sun Ru abandoned Heyang.

sentences.zh: 罕之與言收合其眾，求援於太原，李克用遣澤州刺史安金俊率騎助之，遂收河陽。

translations.literal: Hanzhi and Yan gathered their masses, sought aid from Taiyuan; Li Keyong sent Ze prefecture military commissioner An Jinjun with cavalry to aid them and then recovered Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi and Yan begged Taiyuan; Keyong sent An Jinjun and they retook Heyang.

sentences.zh: 克用表罕之為節度、同平章事；

translations.literal: Keyong memorialized Hanzhi as military commissioner and co-equal chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong made Hanzhi commissioner and chief minister;

sentences.zh: 又表言為河南尹、東都留守。

translations.literal: He also memorialized Yan as Henan prefect and eastern capital acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: and Yan Henan prefect and eastern capital regent.

sentences.zh: 罕之既與言患難交契，刻臂為盟，永同休戚，如張耳、陳餘之義也。

translations.literal: Hanzhi, having with Yan shared hardship and sworn brotherhood, cut arms to covenant, forever sharing fortune and misfortune, like Zhang Er and Chen Yu's righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yan swore blood brotherhood like Zhang Er and Chen Yu.

sentences.zh: 罕之雖有膽決，雄猜翻覆，而撫民禦眾無方略，率多苛暴，性復貪冒，不得士心。

translations.literal: Though Hanzhi had daring resolve and was fierce, suspicious, and changeable, in comforting the people and controlling the masses he had no strategy—mostly harsh and violent, nature again greedy, and could not win officers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Brave yet treacherous and greedy, he ruled without strategy and won no loyalty.

sentences.zh: 既得河陽，出兵攻晉、絳。

translations.literal: Once he had Heyang he sent troops to attack Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then raided Jin and Jiang from Heyang.

sentences.zh: 時大亂之後，野無耕稼，罕之部下以俘剽為資，啖人作食。

translations.literal: At that time after great disorder the wild had no plowing; Hanzhi's subordinates took captives and plunder as resources and ate people as food.
translations.idiomatic: His men lived by capture and cannibalism amid famine.

sentences.zh: 絳州刺史王友遇以城降，罕之乃進攻晉州，河中王重盈遣使求援於太祖。

translations.literal: Jiang prefecture military commissioner Wang Youyu surrendered the city; Hanzhi then advanced to attack Jin prefecture; Hezhong's Wang Chongying sent envoys begging aid from the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: After Youyu surrendered Jiang he besieged Jin; Wang Chongying begged the Founder for aid.

sentences.zh: 時張言治軍有法，善積聚，勤於播植，軍儲不乏。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yan governed troops with method, was good at accumulation, diligent in planting, and army stores did not lack.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan supplied grain efficiently while Hanzhi demanded endlessly.

sentences.zh: 言輸粟於罕之，以給其軍，罕之求索無限，言頗苦之，力不能應，罕之則錄河南府吏笞責之。

translations.literal: Yan transported grain to Hanzhi to supply his army; Hanzhi's demands were without limit; Yan was quite distressed, strength could not answer; Hanzhi then recorded Henan prefecture clerks and flogged and blamed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan could not meet his demands Hanzhi flogged Henan clerks.

sentences.zh: 東諸侯修貢行在，多為罕之邀留，王重盈苦其侵削，密結張言請圖之。

translations.literal: Eastern feudatories sent tribute to the traveling palace; many were detained by Hanzhi; Wang Chongying suffered his encroachments and secretly joined Zhang Yan to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: He seized eastern tribute and Chongying plotted with Yan against him.

sentences.zh: 文德元年春，會罕之盡出其眾攻平陽，言夜出師掩擊河陽，罕之無備，單步僅免，舉族為言所俘。

translations.literal: In spring of Wende year 1, when Hanzhi led out all his masses to attack Pingyang, Yan by night marched troops in ambush strike on Heyang; Hanzhi was unprepared, alone on foot barely escaped, and his whole clan was captured by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Wende 1 spring Yan seized Heyang while Hanzhi attacked Pingyang; Hanzhi fled alone and his clan was captured.

sentences.zh: 罕之奔於太原，李克用表為澤州刺史，仍領河陽節度使。

translations.literal: Hanzhi fled to Taiyuan; Li Keyong memorialized him Ze prefecture military commissioner, still holding Heyang military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing to Taiyuan, Keyong made him Ze prefect while he still claimed Heyang.

sentences.zh: 三月，克用遣其將李存孝率師三萬助之，來攻懷、孟。

translations.literal: In the third month Li Keyong sent his general Li Cunxiao with thirty thousand troops to aid him, coming to attack Huai and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Month 3 Keyong sent Li Cunxiao with thirty thousand against Huai and Meng.

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，備豫皆竭，張言遣其孥入質，且求救於太祖；

translations.literal: In the cities food was exhausted and stores all depleted; Zhang Yan sent his wife and children in as hostages and also begged rescue from the Founder;
translations.idiomatic: Starving, Yan sent hostages and begged the Founder;

sentences.zh: 太祖遣葛從周、牛存節赴之，逆戰於流河店。

translations.literal: The Founder sent Ge Congzhou and Niu Cunjie to go; they met in battle at Liuhe Store.
translations.idiomatic: the Founder sent Ge Congzhou and Niu Cunjie to Liuhe Store.

sentences.zh: 會晉將安休休以一軍奔於蔡，存孝引軍而退，罕之保於澤州。

translations.literal: When Jin general An Xiuxiu with one army fled to Cai, Cunxiao led troops and withdrew; Hanzhi guarded at Ze prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When An Xiuxiu defected to Cai, Cunxiao withdrew and Hanzhi held Ze.

sentences.zh: 自是罕之日以兵寇鈔懷、孟、晉、絳，數百里內，郡邑無長吏，閭裏無居民。

translations.literal: From then Hanzhi daily with troops raided and plundered Huai, Meng, Jin, and Jiang; within several hundred li, prefectures and districts had no long officials, lanes and hamlets no residents.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he ravaged Huai, Meng, Jin, and Jiang until the land lay empty of officials and people.

sentences.zh: 河內百姓，相結屯寨，或出樵汲，即為俘馘。

translations.literal: Hezhong commoners together formed stockaded hamlets; if they went out for fuel or water they became captives.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong peasants who ventured out for fuel or water were taken.

sentences.zh: 雖奇峰絕磴，梯危架險，亦為罕之部眾攻取。

translations.literal: Even strange peaks and sheer cliffs, ladders dangerous and bridges perilous, were also taken by Hanzhi's command masses.
translations.idiomatic: Even mountain strongholds fell to his raiders.

sentences.zh: 先是，蒲、絳之間有山曰摩雲，邑人立柵於上，以避寇亂；

translations.literal: Earlier between Pu and Jiang there was a mountain called Cloud-Touching; townspeople set a stockade on it to avoid bandit disorder;
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Cloud-Touching between Pu and Jiang peasants had built a refuge;

sentences.zh: 罕之以百餘人攻下之，軍中因號罕之為李摩雲。

translations.literal: Hanzhi with a hundred-odd men attacked and took it; in the army they therefore called Hanzhi Li Cloud-Touching.
translations.idiomatic: he took it with a hundred men and was nicknamed Li Cloud-Touching.

sentences.zh: 自是數州之民，屠啖殆盡，荊棘蔽野，煙火斷絕，凡十餘年。

translations.literal: From then the people of several prefectures were slaughtered and eaten nearly clean; brambles covered the wild; smoke and fire cut off—for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years his cannibal raids left the region a dead wilderness.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年，李克用出師以拒邠、鳳，營於渭北，天子以克用為邠州行營四面都統，克用乃表罕之為副。

translations.literal: In Qianning year 2 Li Keyong led troops to resist Bin and Feng, camped north of Wei; the Son of Heaven made Keyong overall commander on four sides for Bin; Keyong then memorialized Hanzhi as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Qianning 2 Keyong campaigned against Bin and Feng and made Hanzhi his deputy.

sentences.zh: 及誅王行瑜，罕之以功授檢校太尉，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Wang Xingyu was executed, Hanzhi for merit was granted honorary Grand Marshal, fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingyu's death Hanzhi became honorary Grand Marshal with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 罕之自以功多，私謂晉將蓋寓曰：「餘自河陽失守，來依巨蔭，歲月滋久，功效未施。

translations.literal: Hanzhi himself thought his merit great and privately told Jin general Gai Yu: "I since losing Heyang have come to rely on great shade; months and years increase yet achievement is not shown.
translations.idiomatic: He told Gai Yu, "Since losing Heyang I have relied on great patronage, yet for years I have shown no achievement.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，倦於師旅，所謂老夫耄矣，無能為也。

translations.literal: In recent years I am weary of campaigns—what is called this old man is aged and cannot act.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years I have wearied of campaigns—this old man is aged and can do no more.

sentences.zh: 望吾王仁湣，太傅哀憐，與一小鎮，休兵養疾，一二年間即歸老菟裘，幸也。」

translations.literal: I hope our prince is benevolent and the Grand Tutor takes pity, gives me a small post, rests troops and heals illness—in one or two years I return old to my rabbit burrow—that would be fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I beg our prince and the Grand Tutor to pity me with a small post to rest my troops and heal my illness—in one or two years I would retire to my rabbit burrow. That would be fortune."

sentences.zh: 寓為言之，克用不對。

translations.literal: Yu spoke for him; Keyong did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Yu pleaded; Keyong was silent.

sentences.zh: 每藩鎮缺帥，議所不及，罕之私心鬱鬱，蓋寓懼其他圖，亟為論之。

translations.literal: Whenever a frontier post lacked a commander, discussion did not reach him; Hanzhi in private was depressed; Gai Yu feared he would plot otherwise and urgently argued for him.
translations.idiomatic: Passed over for every command, he brooded until Gai Yu feared treachery and pleaded again.

sentences.zh: 克用曰：「吾於罕之，豈惜一鎮；

translations.literal: Keyong said: "My toward Hanzhi—how would I begrudge one post;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong said, "It is not that I begrudge him a post;

sentences.zh: 吾有罕之，亦如董卓之有呂布，雄則雄矣，鷹鳥之性，飽則颺去，實懼翻覆毒餘也。」

translations.literal: my having Hanzhi is also like Dong Zhuo's having Lü Bu—fierce he is fierce, but hawk-and-bird nature, sated then flies away; truly I fear he will turn and poison the remainder."
translations.idiomatic: I keep him as Dong Zhuo kept Lü Bu—fierce but untrustworthy when fed."

sentences.zh: 光化元年十二月，晉之潞帥薛誌勤卒，罕之乘其喪，自澤州率眾徑入潞州，自稱留後，以狀聞於克用曰：「聞誌勤之喪，新帥未至，慮為他盜所窺，不俟命，已屯於潞矣。」

translations.literal: Guanghua year 1, twelfth month, Jin's Lu commander Xue Zhiqin died; Hanzhi seized the mourning interval, led his forces from Ze prefecture straight into Lu prefecture, declared himself acting commissioner, and reported to Keyong: "Hearing of Zhiqin's death, the new commander has not arrived; fearing other bandits may spy, without awaiting orders I have already encamped at Lu."
translations.idiomatic: Guanghua 1, month 12, after Xue Zhiqin died as Lu commander, Hanzhi marched from Ze into Lu, declared himself commissioner, and told Keyong, "With Zhiqin dead and no successor yet, I feared raiders and garrisoned Lu without orders."

sentences.zh: 克用怒，遣李昭嗣討之，罕之執其守將馬溉、伊鐸、何萬友，沁州刺史傅瑤等，遣其子顥拘送於太祖以求援焉。

translations.literal: Keyong was angry and sent Li Zhaosi to attack him; Hanzhi seized the garrison commanders Ma Gai, Yi Duo, He Wanyou, Qin prefecture commissioner Fu Yao, and the rest, and sent his son Hao bound to the Founder to beg for aid.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Li Zhaosi against him; Hanzhi seized Ma Gai, Yi Duo, He Wanyou, Fu Yao, and others and sent his son Hao to the Founder for help.

sentences.zh: （《新唐書》：全忠表罕之昭義軍節度使。）

translations.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Quanzhong memorialized Hanzhi as Zhaoyi military commissioner.)
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Quanzhong made Hanzhi Zhaoyi commissioner.)

sentences.zh: 會罕之暴病，不能視事。

translations.literal: When Hanzhi suddenly fell ill he could not handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi then fell suddenly ill and could not govern.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，病篤，太祖令丁會代之，移罕之為河陽節度使；

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the next year, gravely ill, the Founder had Ding Hui replace him and moved Hanzhi to Heyang military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Next year, month 6, the Founder replaced him with Ding Hui and made Hanzhi Heyang commissioner;

sentences.zh: 行至懷州，卒於傳舍，時年五十八。

translations.literal: reaching Huai prefecture he died at the relay station at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: he died at a relay station in Huai at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 其子顥以舟載柩，歸葬河陰縣。

translations.literal: His son Hao carried the coffin by boat and buried him in Heyin county.
translations.idiomatic: Son Hao brought the coffin by boat to bury him in Heyin.

sentences.zh: 開平二年春，詔贈中書令。

translations.literal: In the spring of Kaiping year 2 an edict posthumously made him Chief Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiping 2 spring he was posthumously named Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 馮行襲，字正臣，武當人也。

translations.literal: Feng Xingxi, style name Zhengchen, was a Wudang man.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingxi, styled Zhengchen, came from Wudang.

sentences.zh: 曆職為本郡都校。

translations.literal: He successively served as this prefecture's column commander.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through local command posts.

sentences.zh: 中和中，僖宗在蜀，有賊首孫喜者，聚徒數千人慾入武當，刺史呂煜惶駭無策略。

translations.literal: In Zhonghe, Xizong was in Shu; there was bandit chieftain Sun Xi who gathered followers several thousand wishing to enter Wudang; military commissioner Lü Yu was fearful and alarmed without strategy.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhonghe, bandit Sun Xi threatened Wudang and prefect Lü Yu was helpless.

sentences.zh: 行襲伏勇士於江南，乘小舟逆喜，謂喜曰：「郡人得良牧，眾心歸矣，但緣兵多，民懼擄掠。

translations.literal: Xingxi hid braves south of the river, took a small boat against Xi, and told Xi: "The prefecture people have gained a good shepherd; the masses' hearts turn to him—only because troops are many the people fear plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxi met Xi on the river and told him, "The people have a good shepherd and their hearts have turned to him, but your troops are many and the people fear plunder.

sentences.zh: 若駐軍江北，領肘腋以赴之，使某前導，以安慰士民，可立定也。」

translations.literal: If you camp troops north of the river and lead elbow-and-flank to go to them, let me go before to comfort soldiers and people—it can be settled at once."
translations.idiomatic: If you camp north of the river and let me go ahead to calm soldiers and people, all can be settled at once."

sentences.zh: 喜然之。

translations.literal: Xi was pleased with this.
translations.idiomatic: Xi agreed.

sentences.zh: 既渡江，軍吏迎謁，伏甲奮起，行襲擊喜仆地，仗劍斬之，其黨盡殪，賊眾在江北者悉奔潰。

translations.literal: Once across the river, army clerks welcomed and attended; hidden armor leaped up; Xingxi struck Xi prostrate, sword in hand beheaded him; his party were all slaughtered; bandit masses north of the river all fled routed.
translations.idiomatic: Across the river Xingxi ambushed and beheaded Xi; his band fled.

sentences.zh: 山南節度使劉巨容以功上言，尋授均州刺史。

translations.literal: Shannan military commissioner Liu Jurong memorialized the merit; soon he was appointed Jun prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jurong rewarded him with Jun prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州西有長山，當襄、漢、蜀路，群賊屯據，以邀劫貢奉，行襲又破之。

translations.literal: West of the prefecture was Long Mountain on the Xiang, Han, and Shu road; bandits encamped to intercept and rob tribute; Xingxi again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared Long Mountain bandits who robbed tribute on the road to Shu.

sentences.zh: 洋州節度使葛佐奏辟為行軍司馬，請將兵鎮穀口，通秦、蜀道，由是益知名。

translations.literal: Yangzhou military commissioner Ge Zuo memorialized him as campaign deputy and asked to lead troops to garrison Gukou, opening the Qin-Shu road—from this he grew more famous.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Zuo made him deputy and garrison commander at Gukou on the Shu road.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞遣養子繼臻竊據金州，行襲攻下之，因授金州防禦使。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen sent adopted son Jizhen to steal and hold Jin prefecture; Xingxi attacked and took it and was appointed Jin defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jin from Maozhen's adopted son Jizhen and became Jin commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時興元楊守亮將襲京師，道出金、商，行襲逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: At that time Xingyuan's Yang Shouliang was about to strike the capital; the road passed Jin and Shang; Xingxi met and struck, greatly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed Yang Shouliang marching on the capital through Jin and Shang.

sentences.zh: 詔升金州為節鎮，以戎昭軍為額，即以行襲為節度使。

translations.literal: An edict raised Jin prefecture to a military commission, with Rongzhao army as designation; Xingxi was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was raised to a circuit under Xingxi as Rongzhao commissioner.

sentences.zh: 及太祖義旗西征，行襲遣副使魯崇矩稟受制令。

translations.literal: When the Founder raised his righteous banner west, Xingxi sent deputy Lu Chongju to receive controlled orders.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder marched west, Xingxi sent deputy Lu Chongju for orders.

sentences.zh: 會唐昭宗幸鳳翔，太祖帥師奉迎，久之未出。

translations.literal: When Tang Zhaozong went to Fengxiang, the Founder led troops to welcome him but after long time did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong went to Fengxiang the Founder marched to meet him but lingered outside.

sentences.zh: 中尉韓全誨遣中官郤文晏等二十餘人分命矯詔，欲征江、淮兵屯於金州，以脅太祖之軍，行襲定策盡殺之，收其詔敕送於太祖。

translations.literal: Army Rong Commissioner Han Quanhui sent inner officials Xi Wenyan and more than twenty others with divided forged edicts, wishing to levy Jiang and Huai troops to camp at Jin prefecture and coerce the Founder's army; Xingxi decided on a plan and killed them all, collected their edicts and sent them to the Founder.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanhui sent Xi Wenyan and twenty eunuchs with forged orders to raise Jiang-Huai troops at Jin and threaten the Founder; Xingxi killed them and sent the edicts to the Founder.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年，兼領洋州節度使。

translations.literal: In Tianyou year 1 he added concurrent Yangzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 1 he added Yangzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太祖之伐荊、襄，行襲令其子勖以舟師會於均、房，預收復功，遷匡國軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the Founder attacked Jing and Xiang, Xingxi ordered his son Xu with river forces to join at Jun and Fang, sharing in the recovery merit; he was moved to Kuangguo military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jing-Xiang campaign Xingxi sent son Xu by river to Jun and Fang; rewarded, he became Kuangguo commissioner.

sentences.zh: 到任，誅大吏張澄，暴其罪，州人莫不惴懾。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he executed senior clerk Zhang Cheng, exposed his crimes, and the prefecture people were all fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Taking office he executed clerk Zhang Cheng and terrified the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在許三年，上供外，別進助軍羨糧二十萬石。

translations.literal: At Xu for three years, beyond tribute he separately presented two hundred thousand piculs of surplus grain to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: For three years at Xu he sent two hundred thousand piculs of extra grain beyond tribute.

sentences.zh: 及太祖郊禋，行襲請入覲，貢獻巨萬，恩禮殊厚。

translations.literal: When the Founder performed suburban sacrifice, Xingxi asked to enter court audience, presented gifts worth tens of thousands, and favor and courtesy were exceptionally thick.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban rites Xingxi came to court with lavish gifts and exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 尋詔翰林學士杜曉撰德政碑以賜之，累官至兼中書令，冊拜司空。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered Hanlin academician Du Xiao to compose a merit stele to bestow on him; he rose through offices to concurrent Chief Minister of the Secretariat and was enfeoffed Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xiao wrote his merit stele; he rose to concurrent chief minister and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 開平中卒，輟朝一日，贈太傅，諡曰忠敬。

translations.literal: He died in Kaiping; court mourning ceased one day; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor with posthumous title Loyal and Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kaiping; mourning paused one day; posthumously Grand Tutor, loyal and respectful.

sentences.zh: 行襲性嚴烈，為政深刻，然所至有天幸，境內嘗大蝗，尋有群鳥啄食，不為害；

translations.literal: Xingxi's nature was stern and fierce, government deep and cutting, yet wherever he went there was heaven's luck; within the borders there was once a great locust plague; soon flocks of birds pecked and ate and it did not harm;
translations.idiomatic: Harsh yet lucky, he saw locusts devoured by birds and

sentences.zh: 民或艱食，必有穭穀，出於壟畝。

translations.literal: if the people had hard food, there was always gleaning grain coming from the furrows.
translations.idiomatic: gleanings appear when the people hungered.

sentences.zh: 雖威福在己，而恆竭力以奉於王室，故能保其功名。

translations.literal: Though authority and blessing were in his own hands, he constantly exhausted strength to serve the royal house, and therefore could preserve his fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He used his power to serve the throne and kept his fame.

sentences.zh: 行襲魁岸雄壯，麵有青誌，當時目為「馮青麵」。

translations.literal: Xingxi was tall and imposing, his face had blue marks; men of the time called him "Feng Blue-Face."
translations.idiomatic: Tall and imposing, with a blue mark on his face, he was called "Feng Blue-Face."

sentences.zh: 長子勖，曆蘄、沁二州刺史。

translations.literal: Eldest son Xu successively held Qi and Qin prefecture military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Son Xu governed Qi and Qin.

sentences.zh: 次子德晏，仕至金吾將軍。

translations.literal: Second son Deyan rose to Golden Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Son Deyan became Golden Guard general.

sentences.zh: 孫德昭，鹽州五原縣人，世為州校。

translations.literal: Sun Dezhao was a Wuyuan county man of Yan prefecture; for generations they were prefecture officers.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Dezhao of Wuyuan in Yanzhou came from a line of prefectural officers.

sentences.zh: 父惟晸，有功於唐朝，遙領荊南節度，分判右神策軍事。

translations.literal: His father Weijing had merit toward the Tang house, held Jingnan military commission at a distance, and divided judgment of the Right Shence army affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His father Weijing served Tang with distant Jingnan commission and Shence command.

sentences.zh: 德昭藉父蔭，累職為右神策軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Dezhao relied on father's shade, successively served as Right Shence army overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao inherited rank as Right Shence commander.

sentences.zh: 光化三年，唐昭宗為閹宦所廢，矯立德王，時中外以權在禁闥，莫能致討，近藩朋附，章表繼有至者。

translations.literal: In Guanghua year 3 Tang Zhaozong was deposed by eunuchs, who falsely established Prince De; at that time authority was in the inner court and none could strike in correction; near feudatories attached in factions; memorials continuously arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghua 3 eunuchs deposed Zhaozong and set up Prince De while none could resist.

sentences.zh: 丞相崔胤，外與太祖申結輔佐之好，內遣心腹密講忠義。

translations.literal: Chief minister Cui Yin outwardly with the Founder declared assisting friendship, inwardly sent trusted men secretly to discuss loyal righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin allied with the Founder and secretly plotted restoration.

sentences.zh: 有以事喻德昭者，

translations.literal: There was one who used affairs to persuade Dezhao,
translations.idiomatic: Someone persuaded Dezhao,

sentences.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：德昭常惋不平，崔胤聞之，遣判官石戩與之遊。

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror》: Dezhao often grieved in injustice; Cui Yin heard it and sent aide Shi Kan to roam with him.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says Cui Yin sent Shi Kan to win Dezhao.

sentences.zh: 德昭每酒酣必泣，戩知其誠，乃密以允意說之。）〉

translations.literal: Whenever Dezhao was deep in wine he must weep; Kan knew his sincerity and secretly with consent's intent persuaded him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao wept when drunk; Shi Kan secured his pledge.)〉

sentences.zh: 德昭感慨，乃與本軍孫承誨、董從實三人，奮發應命，誓圖返正，崔又割衣手筆以通其志。

translations.literal: Dezhao was moved and therefore with this army's Sun Chenghui and Dong Congshi three men roused to answer the mandate, swore to plot restoration; Cui again cut robe and wrote by hand to communicate his will.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Dezhao joined Sun Chenghui and Dong Congshi to restore the throne; Cui Yin sealed the pact in writing.

sentences.zh: 天復元年正月一日未旦，逆豎左軍容劉季述早入，德昭伏甲要路以俟，追其前驅，邀而斬之，孫承誨等分捕左軍容王仲先黨伍。

translations.literal: Tianfu year 1, first month, first day before dawn, rebel eunuch Left Army Rong Commissioner Liu Jishu early entered; Dezhao hid armor on the crucial road to wait, pursued his vanguard, intercepted and beheaded him; Sun Chenghui and the rest separately captured Left Army Rong Commissioner Wang Zhongxian's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu 1, New Year's dawn, Dezhao ambushed and killed Liu Jishu; Chenghui seized Wang Zhongxian's faction.

sentences.zh: 唐昭宗方幽辱東內，聞外喧，大恐。

translations.literal: Tang Zhaozong was just humiliated in the eastern inner palace; hearing outer clamor, he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozong, imprisoned in the eastern palace, heard the uproar and feared.

sentences.zh: 德昭馳至，扣閣曰：「逆賊劉季述伏誅矣，請上皇開鑰復皇帝位。」

translations.literal: Dezhao galloped to him, knocked on the gate and said: "Rebel bandit Liu Jishu has submitted to execution—beg the High Sovereign open the lock and restore the Son of Heaven's throne."
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao galloped up, knocked on the gate, and cried, "The rebel Liu Jishu has been executed—open the gate and restore the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 皇后何氏呼曰：「汝可進逆人首，門乃可開。」

translations.literal: Empress He called: "You may advance the rebel's head—then the gate can be opened."
translations.idiomatic: The empress called out, "Bring the rebel's head—then the gate may open."

sentences.zh: 俄而承誨、從實俱以馘獻，昭宗悲而嘉之。

translations.literal: Soon Chenghui and Congshi both presented heads; Zhaozong grieved and praised them.
translations.idiomatic: They brought heads; Zhaozong wept and praised them.

sentences.zh: 於是丞相崔胤奉迎禦丹鳳樓，率百辟待罪，泣且奏曰：「臣居大位，不能討奸，賴東平王全忠首奮忠貞，誅殺邸吏，遂致德昭等擒戮妖逆，再清禁闈。」

translations.literal: Then chief minister Cui Yin welcomed the imperial carriage to Danfeng Tower; led the hundred officials to await guilt, weeping and memorializing: "Your subject occupies great position yet could not strike treachery—dependent on Prince of the East's Zhu Quanzhong first rousing loyal firmness, executing palace clerks, thus causing Dezhao and the rest to capture and slaughter demonic rebels and again clear the forbidden precinct."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin welcomed the emperor to Danfeng Tower, led the officials in self-reproach, and wept as he memorialized, "I held high office yet failed to punish treachery; thanks to Prince of the East Zhu Quanzhong's loyal stand and killing of palace agents, Dezhao and the rest could capture the rebels and clear the palace again."

sentences.zh: 即日議功，以德昭為檢校太保、靜海軍節度使，承誨邕州節度使，從實容州節度使，並同平章事，錫姓李，賜號扶傾濟難忠烈功臣，圖形淩煙閣，俱留京師。

translations.literal: That day merit was discussed; Dezhao was made honorary Grand Guardian, Jinghai military commissioner; Chenghui Yong prefecture commissioner; Congshi Rong prefecture commissioner—all co-equal chief ministers, granted surname Li, bestowed title Upright-Overturning, Calamity-Aiding Loyal Martyr Merit Minister, portraits in Lingyan Pavilion, all kept at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao became honorary Grand Guardian and Jinghai commissioner; his allies received circuits, Li surname, merit titles, and Lingyan portraits.

sentences.zh: 錫賚宴賞之厚，恩寵權幸之勢，近代罕比。

translations.literal: Bestowal, feasts, and rewards were thick; favor and fortune's power—rare in recent generations.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and favor were unmatched in their day.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，閹宦韓全誨縱火脅昭宗西幸鳳翔，承誨、從實並變節，為中官所誘，始欲驅擁百僚，將圖出令。

translations.literal: That year, eleventh month, eunuch Han Quanhui set fire and coerced Zhaozong west to Fengxiang; Chenghui and Congshi both changed sides, enticed by inner officials, at first wishing to drive and crowd the hundred officials and plot to issue orders.
translations.idiomatic: Month 11 Han Quanhui took the emperor to Fengxiang; Chenghui and Congshi turned traitor with the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 而德昭獨按兵，與太祖親吏婁敬思葉力衛丞相及文武百官，與長安吏民保於街東，免為所劫。

translations.literal: Only Dezhao held troops still, with the Founder's personal aide Lou Jingsi strove to guard the chief minister and civil and military officials, with Chang'an clerks and people protecting east of the street, spared from being seized.
translations.idiomatic: Only Dezhao held his troops and with Lou Jingsi shielded Cui Yin and the court east of the street.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣從事相繼勞問，遺以龍鳳劍、鬥雞紗，委令製輯。

translations.literal: The Founder sent staff in succession to comfort and ask, gifted dragon-phoenix sword and fighting-cock gauze, entrusted with restraint and arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder sent gifts and entrusted him to keep order.

sentences.zh: 於是百官次華州，連狀請太祖迎奉。

translations.literal: Then the hundred officials at Huazhou jointly memorialized begging the Founder to welcome and attend.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at Hua begged the Founder to restore the court.

sentences.zh: 及大旆入關，德昭以軍禮上謁，立道左，太祖命左右扶騎控至長安，賜與甚厚，署權知同州節度留後。

translations.literal: When the great banner entered the passes, Dezhao with army rites paid court, stood by the road's left; the Founder ordered attendants to support, mount, and rein-control to Chang'an, gifts very thick, appointed provisional Tongzhou military acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder's banner entered the passes, Dezhao paid his respects with military rites and stood at the left of the road. The Founder ordered attendants to help him mount and escort him by the reins to Chang'an, gave him lavish gifts, and appointed him acting military commissioner of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 將赴任，復徇民請，留充兩街製置使，賜錢百萬。

translations.literal: About to go to his post, again yielding to the people's request, he was kept as two-streets disposition commissioner, granted a million cash.
translations.idiomatic: The people kept him as capital disposition commissioner with a million cash.

sentences.zh: 德昭以本部兵八千人獻於太祖，由是愈見賞重，又賜甲第一區，俾先還洛陽。

translations.literal: Dezhao presented his original command's eight thousand men to the Founder; from this he was even more seen and valued; again given one mansion of armor, ordered first to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He gave eight thousand men to the Founder, received a mansion, and went first to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及昭宗東遷，奏授左威衛上將軍，以疾免，歸於別墅。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong moved east he was memorialized Left Valiant Guard upper general; because of illness released, he returned to his villa.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved east he became Left Valiant Guard general, then retired ill to his villa.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，以左領衛上將軍征赴闕。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he was summoned as Left Collar Guard upper general to audience.
translations.idiomatic: At the abdication he was summoned as Left Collar Guard general.

sentences.zh: 開平四年，拜左金吾大將軍，充街使。

translations.literal: In Kaiping year 4 he was made Left Golden Guard great general, full street commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiping 4 he became Left Golden Guard general and street commissioner.

sentences.zh: 末帝即位，俾將命於兩浙，對見失儀，不果行。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne he was sent on mission to the two Zhe circuits; audience demeanor failed and the journey did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor sent him to Zhe but he failed audience and did not go.

sentences.zh: 尋改授右武衛上將軍，俄復左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Right Martial Guard upper general; soon again Left Golden Guard great general.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to Right Martial Guard, then back to Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，詔贈太傅，輟視朝一日。

translations.literal: He died in office; an edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor and halted court audience one day.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously named Grand Tutor; court mourned one day.

sentences.zh: 天復初，德昭與孫承誨、董從實以返正功，時人呼為「三使相」，恩澤俱冠世。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, Dezhao with Sun Chenghui and Dong Congshi for restoration merit—men of the time called them the "Three Envoy-Chancellors"—grace and favor all topped the age.
translations.idiomatic: With Chenghui and Congshi he was called one of the "Three Envoy-Chancellors" for restoring the throne.

sentences.zh: 及承誨至鳳翔，易名繼誨，從實改名彥弼，皆為李茂貞所養。

translations.literal: When Chenghui reached Fengxiang he changed name to Jihui; Congshi changed name to Yanbi—both were adopted by Li Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui became Jihui and Congshi Yanbi under Maozhen's adoption.

sentences.zh: 後閹官之敗，俱戮於京師。

translations.literal: Later when eunuchs were defeated, all were slaughtered at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later the eunuchs' faction fell and both were killed at the capital.

sentences.zh: 惟德昭克全終始，有所稱雲。

translations.literal: Only Dezhao completed beginning and end and had what was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Only Dezhao died a natural death with honor.

sentences.zh: 趙克裕，河陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Keyu was a Heyang man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Keyu came from Heyang.

sentences.zh: 祖、父皆為軍吏。

translations.literal: Grandfather and father were all army clerks.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather and father were army clerks.

sentences.zh: 克裕少為牙將，好讀書，謹儀範，牧伯皆奇待之。

translations.literal: Keyu in youth was a guard officer, loved reading books, was careful in ritual measure, and military commissioners all treated him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: A guard officer who loved books and decorum, he won every commander's favor.

sentences.zh: 累居右職，擢為虎牢關使。

translations.literal: He successively held right posts and was promoted to Hulao Pass commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to command Hulao Pass.

sentences.zh: 光啟中，蔡寇陷河陽，克裕率所部歸於太祖，隸於宣義軍。

translations.literal: In Guangqi, Cai bandits took Heyang; Keyu led his command to return to the Founder and was attached to the Xuanyi army.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai took Heyang he joined the Founder's Xuanyi army.

sentences.zh: 太祖東征徐、鄆，克裕屢受指顧，無不如意。

translations.literal: The Founder east campaigned Xu and Yan; Keyu repeatedly received direction and care—nothing not as wished.
translations.idiomatic: In eastern campaigns against Xu and Yan he never failed the Founder.

sentences.zh: 數年之內，繼領亳、鄭二州刺史。

translations.literal: Within several years he successively held Bo and Zheng prefecture military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Within years he held Bo and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 時關東藩鎮方為蔡寇所毒，黎元流散，不能相保，克裕妙有農戰之備，復善於綏懷，民賴而獲安者眾。

translations.literal: At that time east-of-the-pass feudatories were just poisoned by Cai bandits; common people scattered in flight and could not protect one another; Keyu was subtle in farming-and-war preparation and again good at soothing and holding—many relied on him and obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: While Cai ravaged the east he fed and protected the people better than other lords.

sentences.zh: 太祖表為河陽節度使、檢校右僕射，尋移理許田，入為金吾衛大將軍、檢校司空。

translations.literal: The Founder memorialized him Heyang military commissioner and honorary Right Vice Director; soon he moved to govern Xu fields, entered as Golden Guard great general and honorary Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He became Heyang commissioner, then governed Xu, and entered court as Golden Guard general and honorary Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 及太祖為元帥，以克裕為元帥府左都押衙，復統六軍，兗州平，命權知泰寧軍留後。

translations.literal: When the Founder was marshal, he made Keyu marshal's headquarters left overall holding ya; again commanded the six armies; when Yan prefecture was pacified he was ordered provisional Taining military acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As marshal's left adjutant and six-army commander he acted as Taining commissioner after Yan fell.

sentences.zh: 數月，暴疾而卒。

translations.literal: Within months he died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 開平初，追贈太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiping he was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Early Kaiping he was posthumously named Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 張慎思，清河人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shensi was a Qinghe man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shensi came from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 自黃巢軍來歸，累授軍職，曆諸軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Returning from Huang Chao's army, he successively received military posts and served as overall commander of various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Defecting from Huang Chao, he rose through commands to overall army commander.

sentences.zh: 從平巢、蔡、兗、鄆，皆著功，表授檢校工部尚書，兼宋州長史。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Chao, Cai, Yan, and Yun, he distinguished himself in merit and was memorialized as honorary Minister of Works and concurrent Song prefecture chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself pacifying Chao, Cai, Yan, and Yun and became honorary Minister of Works and Song chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 光化中，加檢校右僕射，權知亳州。

translations.literal: In Guanghua he was made honorary Right Vice Director and provisional Bo prefecture military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Guanghua he became honorary Right Vice Director and acting Bo commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天復三年，昭宗還長安，以從太祖迎駕功，賜號迎鑾毅勇功臣，尋除汝州防禦使。

translations.literal: Tianfu year 3, when Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, for merit in following the Founder to welcome the imperial carriage he was granted the title Welcome-the-Carriage, Resolute-and-Brave Merit Minister; soon he was made Ruzhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu 3, for welcoming the emperor with the Founder, he received the title Welcome-the-Carriage Merit Minister and became Ruzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年，授左龍武統軍。

translations.literal: In Tianyou year 1 he was appointed Left Dragon Martial army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyou 1 he became Left Dragon Martial commander.

sentences.zh: 其冬，除許州匡國軍節度使。

translations.literal: That winter he was made Xu prefecture Kuangguo military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he became Xu Kuangguo commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年十一月，權知徐州武寧軍兩使留後。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the next year he was provisional acting commissioner of Xuzhou Wuning military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, month 11, he acted as Xuzhou Wuning commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，入為左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication he entered as Left Golden Guard great general.
translations.idiomatic: At the abdication he entered as Left Golden Guard great general.

sentences.zh: 開平二年，除宋州刺史，未幾，復拜左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: Kaiping year 2 he was made Song prefecture military commissioner; soon he was again appointed Left Golden Guard great general.
translations.idiomatic: Kaiping 2 he governed Song, then again became Left Golden Guard great general.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，除蔡州刺史，以貪貨大失民情，詔追赴闕。

translations.literal: Winter of year 3 he was made Cai prefecture military commissioner; for greedy seizure of goods he greatly lost the people's hearts and an edict recalled him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Winter, year 3, as Cai commissioner greed cost him popular support and he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 未幾，扈從北征還，以疾臥洛陽之私第。

translations.literal: Soon, returning from escorting the northern campaign, he lay ill in a private residence at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after returning from the northern campaign he fell ill at his Luoyang home.

sentences.zh: 馭家不肅，為其子所弒。

translations.literal: He did not keep his household in order and was murdered by his son.
translations.idiomatic: His household discipline failed and his son murdered him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：韓建遇唐朝之衰運，據潼關之要地，不能藩屏王室，翻務斫喪宗枝，雖有阜俗之能，何補不臣之咎。

translations.literal: The historian says: Han Jian met the Tang house's declining fortune, held Tong Pass's crucial ground, could not screen and protect the royal house, instead devoted himself to cutting off and destroying the imperial branches—though he had ability to enrich customs, how does it repair the fault of disloyalty?
translations.idiomatic: The historian condemns Han Jian for holding Tong Pass yet harming the Tang house despite local good rule.

sentences.zh: 罕之負驍雄之氣，蓄向背之謀，武皇比之呂布，斯知人矣。

translations.literal: Hanzhi bore fierce valor's spirit and stored facing-and-turning plots; the Martial Emperor compared him to Lü Bu—he knew the man.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong rightly compared Hanzhi to Lü Bu.

sentences.zh: 行襲勵納忠之節，德昭立反正之功，俱善其終，固其宜矣。

translations.literal: Xingxi encouraged loyal submission's integrity; Dezhao established restoration's merit; both completed their ends well—it is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxi and Dezhao served loyally and ended well, as they should.

sentences.zh: 克裕而下，無譏可也。

translations.literal: Keyu and below—no reproach is possible.
translations.idiomatic: Keyu and the rest merit no reproach.
